# New-ZbxMapLine

## SYNOPSIS

Builds a map line for the -Line of New-ZbxMap and Set-ZbxMap.

## SYNTAX

```
New-ZbxMapLine [-X1 <int>] [-Y1 <int>] [-X2 <int>] [-Y2 <int>] [-LineType <ZabbixMapShapeBorderType>] [-LineWidth <int>] [-LineColor <string>] [-ZIndex <int>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A line is a drawn line on a network map, independent of any element. The New-ZbxMapLine cmdlet writes it as a hashtable keyed by the API's field names, which the -Line of New-ZbxMap and Set-ZbxMap take as it is, alone or in an array. Nothing is sent to the server, so the command needs no connection.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Build a line and use it in a new map

```powershell
$divider = New-ZbxMapLine -X1 10 -Y1 50 -X2 590 -Y2 50 -LineType Solid -LineWidth 2 -LineColor '336699'
New-ZbxMap -Name 'Office map' -Width 600 -Height 400 -Line $divider | Select-Object MapId, Name
```

The builder writes one line hashtable: the two end points (-X1/-Y1, -X2/-Y2), style, width and hex colour. New-ZbxMap sends it in -Line.

### Example 2: Replace the lines of an existing map

```powershell
$lines = @(
    New-ZbxMapLine -X1 300 -Y1 60 -X2 300 -Y2 390 -LineType Dashed -LineWidth 1 -LineColor '999999'
    New-ZbxMapLine -X1 10 -Y1 50 -X2 590 -Y2 50 -LineType Solid -LineWidth 2 -LineColor '336699'
)
$null = Set-ZbxMap -InputObject 'Office map' -Line $lines
(Get-ZbxMap -Name 'Office map' -SelectLines).Lines | Format-Table x1, y1, x2, y2, line_type, line_color
```

Set-ZbxMap -Line replaces all of the map's lines; -SelectLines reads them back (x1, y1, x2, y2, line_type ...).
